newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil delays civil service reform vote until Wed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil delays civil service reform vote until Wed.

text.p: The Brazilian government's civil service reform bill will be put to a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday, the government's chief whip in the lower house Deputy Benito Gama said.
The bill, which had been scheduled for a vote Tuesday, was still subject to last-minute negotiations, Gama told reporters.
But whips had reached a formula that would prove acceptable to both the government and lawmakers upset over a proposed ceiling on pay and pensions, he said.

Under the proposal, lawmakers, government ministers and personal aides of senior civil servants would be allowed to hold on to one pension, even if it took them over a proposed 10,800-reais ($10,180) monthly ceiling on pay and pensions.
Opposition within Congress forced the government to scrap two previous attempts to hold a vote on the bill.
As a constitutional amendment, it requires two three-fifths majorities in each house of Congress.
Civil service reform is considered a key tool for the government's drive to reduce public spending and narrow Brazil's public sector deficit.
